description: deixis N[T] navigation vectors — at, valueAt and the path laws of ADR 0009 §5 (S0, S1, S2; missing paths refuse and never create a node or choose a fallback). Hand-authored from docs/design/0009-optional-node-values.md alone, per vectors/NODE-PLAN.md; not generated by an implementation, and replayed against the four cores by tools/conformance/harness.mjs. Spelling as in NODE-PLAN.md. A path is a list of hex keys; [] is the empty path ε. A defined `at` result is a node, compared with the structural equality of node-identity.json; a defined `valueAt` result is {none:{}} or {some:<payload>}, compared under ≈. `at-compose` checks S1 by navigating `first`, then `then`, from the result. Under ADR 0010 this file reads as the explicit optional instantiation Node[Option[fixture]], with the tag-respecting option slot of vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md; every case here holds there under the mandatory core's generic laws (checked case by case on 2026-09-23; see NODE-PLAN.md).

cases.name: valueAt-root-unvalued-is-none-not-undefined
cases.note: X2. §5: valueAt returns None for an existing unvalued node.

cases.name: valueAt-valued-root-with-children
cases.note: X1. A node can have an own value and children at once (§3); the value is readable at its own path.

cases.name: valueAt-missing-child-is-undefined
cases.note: X4. §5: valueAt is undefined for a missing node. An absent node is not an unvalued node, so returning None would be wrong.

cases.name: at-missing-child-refuses-rather-than-creating
cases.note: C10. §5: missing paths refuse; they neither create nodes nor choose a fallback. A map-backed at() that auto-vivifies and returns Node(None,{}) fails here.

cases.name: at-missing-grandchild-refuses
cases.note: C10 at depth two. The first step exists and the second does not; the whole navigation is undefined, not the deepest existing node.

cases.name: at-empty-key-child
cases.note: X5. The path [""] has length one and differs from ε (§3). (S2) at(n,[k]) is defined iff k ∈ dom(children(n)), and "" is in the domain.

cases.name: at-empty-key-absent-when-only-zero-byte-key-exists
cases.note: X5/C4. The empty key and the key 00 are different byte strings; (S2) needs "" itself in the domain.

cases.name: valueAt-root-and-empty-key-child-are-different-positions
cases.note: X5. The value at [""] is the child's (class 7), not the root's (class 8). An implementation that collapses the empty key onto the empty path returns 8.

cases.name: at-compose-matches-concatenated-path
cases.note: X6. (S1) at(at(n,p),q) ≡ at(n,p ++ q); the expected value is the at-deep-path result.

cases.name: at-compose-undefined-on-both-sides
cases.note: X6. §5: partial equations require equal definedness. at(n,[k,j]) is undefined, so the composed navigation must be undefined too.

cases.name: valueAt-valued-interior-node
cases.note: X1/X9. A value at a node that has descendants. In the old model a valued position is terminal (§4); in N it is not.

cases.name: at-through-a-valued-node
cases.note: X9. Navigation passes through a valued node to its child. An implementation that treats a valued node as a leaf refuses here.

cases.name: valueAt-unvalued-child-of-valued-node
cases.note: X2. The child exists and is unvalued, so the result is None. It does not inherit the parent's value.

cases.name: at-non-utf8-key
cases.note: X5. A key that is not valid UTF-8 navigates like any other (K = Bytes).

cases.name: at-key-prefix-is-not-the-key
cases.note: X5/C4. The one-byte key ff is a prefix of the key ff00 and is not in the domain; (S2) is exact.

cases.name: at-key-differing-only-in-ascii-case
cases.note: C4. 'K' (4b) is not 'k' (6b). Keys are exact bytes.

cases.name: at-never-enters-a-value
cases.note: C8 at navigation. The own value's representation spells a tree with a child 6b, but resolution walks children only (§5; PATH.md: resolution never enters a value). The node has no children, so [6b] is undefined.
